# Install & Update R Packages {#sec-install-update-r-packages}

> **Learning Objectives:** After this chapter you will be able to:
>
> - Install a package from CRAN with `install.packages()`.
> - Explain the difference between installing and loading a package.
> - Load a package with `library()` in each R session.
> - Update installed packages with `update.packages()`.
> - Fix a "there is no package called" error.

## Introduction

Packages add functions and data to R. Install a package once on your computer, then load it in each R session where you want to use it.

## Install Packages

### CRAN

Packages from CRAN can be installed using `install.packages()`. The name of the package must be enclosed in single or double quotes.

```{r install1, eval=FALSE}
install.packages('ggplot2')
```

## Load a package

`install.packages()` saves a package on your computer. `library()` makes it available in the current R session. You do not need to reinstall a package each time you open R, but you do need to load it again.

```{r package-load, eval=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
```

If `library(ggplot2)` reports `there is no package called 'ggplot2'`, install it with `install.packages("ggplot2")`, then run `library(ggplot2)` again.

## Update Packages

Use `update.packages()` to check for and install updates to your installed packages.

```{r package-update, eval=FALSE}
update.packages()
```
